definition: Raising equipment, floors, foundations or structures above expected flood levels. Does not include barriers, drainage or cable protection.
Building or enlarging drains, culverts or other drainage so that water does not reach or damage the infrastructure. Does not include elevation, barriers or cable protection.
Barriers, walls, embankment protection, or sealed and waterproof enclosures that keep flood water out of facilities. Does not include elevation, drainage, or protection of cables.

Physically protecting cables against hazards with reinforced, armoured or waterproof cables, ducts and conduits, or deeper trenches. Does not include the choice to bury a cable instead of hanging it (that is climate-informed siting), or protection of buildings and equipment.
Strengthening towers, masts, structures or overhead lines against high winds, cyclones and storms. Does not include flood protection or cable ducts.
Protecting equipment or structures against extreme heat (heat-tolerant components, shading, thermal design). Does not include energy-efficient cooling for its own sake.
Structural reinforcement, foundations or slope works against earthquakes, landslides or erosion. Does not include flood or wind protection.
Enclosures, materials and coatings that protect equipment from rain, dust, humidity or corrosion in normal severe weather. Does not include protection against flood water or cable protection.
Physically protects infrastructure from inundation with barriers, sealing or waterproof ducts, other than by elevation or drainage
Strengthens structures against high winds or storms
Protects equipment or structures against extreme temperatures
Strengthens foundations, structures, ducts or other physical components against hazards other than wind
